intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's culinary soul.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Exploration
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's iconic Electric Town, visiting multi-floor electronics shops, retro game arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Experience the epicenter of Japan's otaku and tech culture, including hands-on demos at flagship electronics retailers like Yodobashi Camera.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, wandering through the Nakamise shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks. Explore the surrounding Asakusa district to witness rickshaws, geisha culture remnants, and beautifully preserved Edo-period architecture.

experiences.name: Shibuya and Harajuku Street Food and Fashion Culture Tour
experiences.description: Experience the sensory overload of Shibuya Crossing, then head to Takeshita Street in Harajuku for crepes, rainbow cotton candy, and unique street food. Observe Tokyo's vibrant youth culture, avant-garde fashion, and the intersection of pop culture and culinary creativity.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the world-renowned teamLab Borderless, a groundbreaking digital art museum blending technology, nature, and interactive installations. This one-of-a-kind experience perfectly merges Tokyo's tech innovation with artistic culture, featuring rooms of flowing light, interactive projections, and AI-driven environments.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to hotel in Tsukiji, Chuo City (approx 1–1.5 hrs via Narita Express or Keikyu Line + subway). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Tsukiji Outer Market on foot — browse fresh seafood stalls, tamagoyaki shops, and kitchen tool vendors. Pick up affordable street snacks. Get oriented with the neighborhood and grab a Suica/Pasmo IC card at the station for cheap transit.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji and Hamarikyu Gardens (exterior view is free). Head to nearby Ginza backstreets to window-shop and people-watch. Return to Tsukiji area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport snack)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bowl of ramen or a convenience store bento (7-Eleven / FamilyMart) near Tsukiji — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area — try a fresh sushi set or seafood donburi at one of the small standing sushi bars for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Priority on arrival day: get your IC card, locate the nearest convenience store and coin laundry, and rest early to beat jet lag. April in Tokyo is cherry blossom season — check bloom status!

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — a beautiful traditional garden with tidal ponds and teahouse, right next to the hotel. If cherry blossoms are still blooming, this is a stunning spot. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's tech and anime hub. Browse multi-floor electronics stores (Yodobashi Camera, BIC Camera), retro game shops, and gadget stalls. Many shops have free entry and browsing is free.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and explore the evening neon atmosphere. Visit a maid café for the cultural experience (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a drink + performance). Walk through the illuminated streets.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (onigiri + coffee) near hotel — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a curry rice set lunch at a local curry chain (CoCo Ichibanya) — ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Akihabara — ramen or gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Matsuya — ¥500–¥800

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Many electronics stores have tax-free counters for tourists — bring your passport. Free Wi-Fi available at many spots.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Asakusa — Tokyo's most iconic traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry) and the Nakamise shopping street for cheap traditional souvenirs (keychains, fans, snacks from ¥100).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ueno Park (10 min from Asakusa) — free outdoor park perfect for a stroll. Visit the Tokyo National Museum exterior or explore the park's market stalls. If cherry blossoms remain, Ueno Park is one of the best spots in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market with cheap street food, clothing, and goods. Great for budget shopping and authentic local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa — grab freshly made ningyo-yaki (small sweet cakes) and green tea from a Nakamise stall — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Ueno area — try a teishoku (set meal) at a local diner near the park — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market — grilled seafood skewers, takoyaki, or a cheap sushi plate from market stalls — ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free but can be crowded. Arrive before 9am for a quieter experience. The Nakamise street opens around 10am. Ameyoko is busiest and most fun on Friday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Harajuku — take the train to Harajuku Station and walk through Takeshita Street, famous for quirky fashion, crepes, and youth culture. Great for people-watching and free browsing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) — a serene forested Shinto shrine in the heart of the city. Then stroll through Yoyogi Park, which is especially lively on weekends with performers and picnickers.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya — walk the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing (free, iconic). Visit the free observation deck at Shibuya Sky's rival — the rooftop of Shibuya Hikarie (free floors) or simply enjoy the crossing from street level.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku — a famous Harajuku crepe from a street stall (strawberry + cream) — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Yoyogi Park area — convenience store picnic lunch enjoyed in the park — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Shibuya — try a hearty tonkatsu (pork cutlet) set meal at a local chain like Saboten — ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Harajuku and Shibuya is very busy. Yoyogi Park is free and excellent for a relaxing picnic. Meiji Shrine inner garden has a small fee (¥500) but the main shrine is free.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — a futuristic artificial island with tech museums and waterfront views. Visit teamLab Borderless (digital art museum, book in advance — ¥3,200) or browse the free DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and its giant Gundam statue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Odaiba waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Visit the free Fuji TV building exterior and the Toyota Mega Web (free car showroom with tech exhibits).
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Head to Shiodome or Shimbashi area (close to Tsukiji) for dinner — a salaryman district with many cheap izakayas.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Odaiba — food court at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza — ramen or udon set — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Shimbashi izakaya — order yakitori skewers and a draft beer; set meals available — ¥1,200–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless must be booked online in advance. The Yurikamome monorail to Odaiba is scenic but slightly pricier — use your IC card. Free alternatives in Odaiba make this a very budget-friendly day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Walk through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, old temples, and a historic cemetery. Completely free and very local.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nezu Shrine (free entry) — a smaller but beautiful shrine with hundreds of torii gates, similar to Fushimi Inari in Kyoto but far less crowded. Walk through the tunnel of gates.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji or Shimokitazawa by train — bohemian neighborhoods with vintage shops, live music venues, and cheap local bars. Great for experiencing Tokyo's underground culture scene.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza — fresh melon bread or korokke (croquette) from a local bakery stall — ¥200–¥400
meals.lunch: Yanaka area — a small local soba restaurant, handmade cold soba set — ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — cheap curry or a small ramen shop popular with locals — ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored slowly on foot. Bring cash as many small shops don't accept cards. Nezu Shrine is far less touristy than Senso-ji and a hidden gem.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (if not done yet — book online, ¥3,200) OR explore the Toyosu Market (the new wholesale fish market) — free outer viewing decks of tuna auctions available (register in advance online).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ginza — Tokyo's upscale shopping district. Window-shopping and people-watching are free. Visit the free Itoya stationery flagship store, browse the Apple Store, and check out the free Ginza Six rooftop garden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji for a relaxed evening at the Outer Market — some stalls serve dinner. Walk along the Sumida River at night for beautiful city light reflections.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tamagoyaki roll and miso soup — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Toyosu area — try a fresh sashimi set at a market-adjacent restaurant — ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Ginza backstreet standing bar (tachinomi) — small plates and a beer — ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu tuna auction viewing requires advance registration on the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website. Spots are limited and fill up fast. Ginza is expensive to shop but free to explore.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku — start with the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory (free, opens 9:30am) for panoramic 360° views of Tokyo and Mt. Fuji on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — one of Tokyo's best parks, perfect for a relaxing afternoon walk. Late April may still have some late-blooming cherry blossoms or fresh greenery.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku's famous Golden Gai — a maze of tiny bars with enormous character. Many bars have a small cover charge (¥500–¥1,000) but drinks are affordable. Also walk through Kabukicho entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Shinjuku — a cheap lunch set at a gyudon chain or standing soba shop near the station — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Golden Gai or nearby Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — grilled yakitori skewers and beer in a tiny atmospheric alley bar — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: The Metropolitan Government Building has two towers — both are free. Go on a clear morning for the best chance of seeing Mt. Fuji. Omoide Yokocho is cash only and very atmospheric at night.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approx 2 hrs by train from Asakusa via Tobu Nikko Line — budget ¥1,400 one way). Visit the UNESCO-listed Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate and deeply historical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — walk to Rinno-ji Temple and Futarasan Shrine. Enjoy the forested mountain scenery and waterfalls nearby (Kegon Falls is a short bus ride away).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Grab dinner near Asakusa or Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Pack a convenience store breakfast to eat on the train — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Nikko — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a local specialty, at a small restaurant near the shrines — ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Asakusa area on return — cheap tempura donburi at a local diner — ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: The Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa is the most budget-friendly option. A 2-day pass is available if you plan to stay longer. Nikko shrine entry combo ticket costs ¥1,300. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Akihabara more deeply — visit the free floors of Yodobashi Akiba, browse retro game shops like Super Potato, and check out the free Gundam Café area. Visit a multi-floor manga/anime shop like Mandarake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kanda and Jimbocho — Tokyo's famous secondhand bookstore district. Browse hundreds of cheap used books, vintage maps, and manga. Many English books available too. Completely free to browse.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Kanda Myojin Shrine (free) — a beautiful shrine that is also the spiritual home of IT and tech companies in Japan (many tech firms visit for blessings). Explore the surrounding old neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji area — fresh fish onigiri from a market stall — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a hearty katsu curry at a local lunch spot — ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Kanda — an old-school izakaya near Kanda Station, popular with office workers — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Jimbocho is a must for book lovers and culture enthusiasts. Friday evening izakayas in Kanda are lively and very local. Kanda Myojin has a fascinating connection to Tokyo's tech industry — look for the IT company ema plaques.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno (¥630 entry) — excellent exhibits on Japanese technology, natural history, and science. Very budget-friendly for the content offered.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara's Maid Café district for a second visit or explore the Ochanomizu area — known for music instrument shops, university culture, and the scenic Kanda River. Browse guitar shops and music gear stores.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ikebukuro — another major hub with Sunshine City mall (free to enter), a large Animate anime store, and the free observation area at Sunshine 60 building lobby. Very local feel compared to Shibuya.

meals.breakfast: Ueno area — a cheap morning teishoku set at a neighborhood diner — ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Ochanomizu — a student-friendly cheap curry or ramen restaurant near the universities — ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Ikebukuro — try a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant, plates from ¥110–¥200 each — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Nature and Science is one of the best value museums in Tokyo. Ochanomizu is especially lively on weekends with street musicians. Ikebukuro's Sunshine City has a free rooftop garden.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Digital Art Museum (if not yet visited) OR explore the free Mori Art Museum observation deck in Roppongi Hills (¥1,800 includes gallery access) for sweeping city views and contemporary art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's free outdoor art installations and the National Art Center Tokyo (free permanent collection, special exhibitions vary). Walk through the upscale Azabu-Juban neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Final big dinner night — head to Tsukiji Outer Market for a farewell seafood feast. Try a premium but still budget-friendly sushi omakase at a standing sushi counter (¥2,000–¥3,000 for a full set).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area — convenience store breakfast with premium coffee — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Roppongi / Azabu-Juban — a local ramen shop or cheap lunch bento from a neighborhood deli — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market — standing sushi counter omakase set with fresh market fish — ¥2,000–¥3,000

day_by_day.notes: The National Art Center Tokyo has free admission to its permanent collection and architecture (designed by Kisho Kurokawa) — worth visiting even without paying for special exhibitions. Book Tsukiji sushi early as popular counters fill up.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit a favorite neighborhood or any missed spots. Consider a peaceful early morning walk through Hamarikyu Gardens one last time or a final stroll through Tsukiji Outer Market for breakfast and last-minute edible souvenirs (dried seaweed, tea, snacks).
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and check out of hotel. Head to airport (allow 2–2.5 hrs travel time). Take the Narita Express or Keikyu Line from nearby stations. Use remaining IC card balance at convenience stores or vending machines.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — a final fresh sushi breakfast or tamagoyaki sandwich — ¥600–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Airport — use remaining yen at airport ramen or soba restaurant — ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: In-flight

day_by_day.notes: Refund remaining IC card balance at airport or major station (small ¥220 handling fee). Duty-free shopping available at Narita and Haneda. Keep receipts for tax-free purchases — you may need to show them at the airport. Arrive at airport at least 3 hours before international departure.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji. Check in to your boutique hotel and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market, which remains a vibrant street food and seafood shopping hub. Browse fresh fish stalls, kitchen supply shops, and local vendors. Pick up a tamagoyaki (rolled omelette) or fresh sushi bite as a welcome snack.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (closes at 17:00 — aim to arrive by 15:30 if energy allows) for a serene traditional garden experience beside Tokyo Bay. Then head to Ginza for a relaxed first evening dinner.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab an onigiri and green tea from a convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the airport or hotel
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick snack at Tsukiji Outer Market — try fresh tuna sushi or grilled scallops from a market stall (¥500–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Sushi Zanmai in Tsukiji — a beloved mid-range sushi chain famous for fresh fish, set menus from ¥2,000–¥4,000

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may be a factor. Keep Day 1 light and low-key. Buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. Exchange some yen at the airport for best convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market early (opens around 5:00–6:00 AM) for the full morning market experience. Sample fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, and grilled seafood from vendors. Browse the knife and kitchenware shops — a great spot for food culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) via the Hibiya or Yamanote Line. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Kaikan. Dive into retro gaming arcades, anime merchandise shops, and the latest tech gadgets — a paradise for tech culture lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and explore the maid café culture (try a themed café experience for a uniquely Tokyo moment), then visit a multi-floor arcade like Taito Station for evening entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh tuna don (tuna rice bowl) at Tsukiji Tamai or Nakamura (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.lunch: Ramen at Akihabara's Fuunji or try Curry Udon at a local Akihabara eatery (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba near Akihabara — a historic soba restaurant with handmade noodles, set meals around ¥1,500–¥3,000

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on weekends when some streets close to traffic, but weekdays are less crowded and equally rich. Many electronics shops offer tax-free shopping for tourists — bring your passport.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Asakusa and visit Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early to beat crowds. Walk through Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional souvenirs, ningyo-yaki cakes, and senbei crackers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Sumida River via the Azuma Bridge for views of the Tokyo Skytree, then take the train to Skytree Station. Visit Tokyo Skytree (Tembo Deck at 350m — ¥2,100). Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at its base, which has excellent local food floors and tech/lifestyle shops.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Asakusa entertainment district — visit Hoppy Street for an izakaya dinner experience with locals in a casual, convivial atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa Imahan or a local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near your hotel for a morning set — coffee, toast, and egg (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Tempura Daikokuya in Asakusa — a legendary tempura restaurant established in 1887, lunch sets ¥1,800–¥3,000
meals.dinner: Hoppy Street izakaya (Nakamise Izakaya area) — order hoppy beer, yakitori skewers, and oden, budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: April is cherry blossom season — Sumida Park along the river near Asakusa is one of Tokyo's top hanami (blossom viewing) spots. Bring a picnic snack and enjoy if blossoms are still in bloom.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Harajuku and explore Meiji Jingu Shrine, a peaceful forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Walk the long gravel path through towering torii gates and cedar trees — a spiritual contrast to the city's energy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit Meiji Jingu and walk down Takeshita Street for Tokyo's famous youth fashion culture — quirky fashion, crepe shops, and pop culture stores. Then head to nearby Omotesando for upscale boutiques and the architecturally stunning Omotesando Hills mall.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Shibuya (10 minutes from Harajuku). Witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at dusk — one of the world's busiest pedestrian crossings. Head to the Shibuya Sky rooftop observation deck (¥2,000) for a stunning panoramic night view.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel or Tsukiji Morning Market — onigiri, miso soup cup, and coffee (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Harajuku Gyoza Lou — a beloved local gyoza spot with queues worth waiting for, budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Shibuya Nonbei Yokocho (Drunkard's Alley) — a narrow lantern-lit alley of tiny izakayas and yakitori bars, great for atmosphere and local food, ¥2,500–¥4,000

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Takeshita Street will be very busy — visit early afternoon to manage crowds. Shibuya Scramble is most dramatic at night with neon lights. Book Shibuya Sky tickets online in advance to secure a slot.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the driverless Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi for spectacular bay views. Visit teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (book in advance) — immersive digital art installations blending tech and culture perfectly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (featuring a life-size Gundam statue — a tech/pop culture icon), then visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) for cutting-edge robotics, AI, and space exploration exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Take the water bus back across Tokyo Bay toward Asakusa or Hinode Pier for scenic bay views at sunset. Return to Tsukiji area for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things in Odaiba or grab a quick breakfast at Shimbashi station before boarding the monorail (¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Odaiba Decks Tokyo Beach food floor — try conveyor belt sushi at Uobei or ramen at one of the food court restaurants (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area dinner — Tsukiji Sushiko or a local tonkatsu restaurant near the hotel (¥1,800–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets MUST be booked online well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. Miraikan is excellent for tech enthusiasts and has English signage throughout. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a highlight with sweeping Rainbow Bridge views.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno Park, a vast cultural hub. Explore the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's oldest and largest museum) — housing samurai armor, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, Buddhist sculptures, and ancient artifacts. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Ueno Park (cherry blossoms may still be visible in early-mid April). Visit Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko) Market — a bustling open-air market street beneath the elevated train tracks selling fresh food, clothing, cosmetics, and snacks at bargain prices.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Koenji or Shimokitazawa (bohemian neighborhoods) for Tokyo's indie music and vintage culture scene. Browse vintage clothing shops and catch live music at a small venue if available.

meals.breakfast: Ueno area kissaten or Doutor Coffee for a Japanese-style morning set (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market lunch — try fresh seafood rice bowls, Korean food stalls, or gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya/Matsuya for a budget-friendly authentic experience (¥700–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — Tengu (izakaya chain) or a local curry restaurant; Shimokitazawa has excellent Japanese curry houses (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is one of Tokyo's most famous hanami spots — if blossoms remain, the park will be lively with picnickers. Ameyoko Market is closed on some Wednesdays — Monday is a great day to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours from Tokyo via Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine — an extraordinarily ornate mausoleum complex for Tokugawa Ieyasu, surrounded by cedar forests and featuring the famous 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkey carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Nikko National Park area — visit Rinnoji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and walk the cedar-lined Omotesando approach. If time allows, take a bus to Kegon Falls (97m waterfall) and Lake Chuzenji.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Relax with a quiet dinner near the hotel in Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or convenience store before departure (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Nikko Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a Nikko specialty. Try Gyoshintei restaurant or a local shokudo (diner) in Nikko town (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Back in Tsukiji — Tsukiji Itadori or a nearby soba restaurant for a simple, satisfying meal (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko Pass (¥4,780 round trip including unlimited bus rides in Nikko) for the best value. Start early — aim to depart by 7:30–8:00 AM from Asakusa to maximize time in Nikko. Nikko is a full-day commitment.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved old downtown (shitamachi) neighborhoods. Walk through Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful during cherry blossom season), browse the charming Yanaka Ginza shopping street with traditional craft shops, pottery, and local snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Nezu Shrine — a smaller, photogenic shrine with a tunnel of red torii gates (a less crowded alternative to Fushimi Inari in Kyoto). Then head to Akihabara for a deeper tech culture dive — visit the Akihabara Garage (indie electronics makers space) or Super Potato retro game store.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Tokyo Anime Center or explore Akihabara's evening neon atmosphere. Return to Ginza for an upscale evening stroll along the illuminated shopping boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka bakery breakfast — Kayaba Coffee (a historic 1938 kissaten in Yanaka) for coffee and tamago sando (egg sandwich) (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food — try menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet) from Nakamuraya or croquettes from local vendors (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Ginza Six food floors or Ginza Corridor izakaya street — try yakitori and Japanese whisky at a mid-range izakaya (¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is a wonderful antidote to Tokyo's modernity — carry cash as many small shops don't accept cards. Nezu Shrine's torii tunnel is best photographed in early morning or late afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku — start with Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Japan's most beautiful parks with French, English, and Japanese garden sections. Perfect for a morning walk (especially if late cherry blossoms or early azaleas are blooming, ¥500 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's tech and electronics district around Yodobashi Camera Akiba and Bic Camera. Visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for a free observation deck with panoramic city views. Explore the labyrinthine Shinjuku Station (world's busiest station) as a cultural experience in itself.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane / Piss Alley) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori and ramen stalls under the train tracks near Shinjuku Station West Exit. Then head to Kabukicho for Tokyo's famous nightlife district atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Shinjuku kissaten — Cafe de Lambre (legendary coffee shop) for hand-drip coffee and toast (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Takashimaya Times Square food hall basement (depachika) — pick from dozens of Japanese food counters, sushi, bento, and prepared foods (¥1,000–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori stall — charcoal-grilled chicken skewers, beer, and smoky atmosphere, budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free and offers views comparable to paid towers — a great budget-friendly option. Omoide Yokocho is cash only and extremely atmospheric at night.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (1 hour from Tokyo via JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in) — a 13-meter bronze seated Buddha statue from 1252. Explore Kotoku-in temple grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through forested hills connecting temples. Visit Engaku-ji and Kencho-ji Zen temples — two of Kamakura's most significant Zen Buddhist sites with stunning architecture and peaceful gardens. Browse Komachi-dori Street for local crafts and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo and enjoy a relaxed evening in the Tsukiji/Ginza neighborhood. Optional: visit Ginza's art galleries (many are free and open late on Fridays).

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast or hotel before departure (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Kamakura local specialty — Shirasudon (whitebait rice bowl) at Kaiko-an or Inamuragasaki Shokudo near the beach (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area — try a kaiseki-style set meal at a local restaurant for a cultural dining experience (¥3,000–¥5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Use a JR Pass if you have one, or buy a day return ticket (approx. ¥1,490 each way). Kamakura is hilly — wear comfortable walking shoes. Arrive early on weekends as it gets crowded; Friday is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Roppongi — visit the Mori Art Museum on the 53rd floor of Mori Tower (contemporary art with city views, ¥1,800). The adjacent Tokyo City View observation deck offers 360-degree panoramas. Roppongi Hills complex has excellent architecture and public art installations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi (free entry to permanent collection, one of Japan's largest exhibition spaces). Then head to Daikanyama and Nakameguro — Tokyo's most stylish neighborhoods for boutique shopping, café culture, and design.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Meguro River in Nakameguro — one of Tokyo's most romantic evening strolls (especially beautiful if late cherry blossoms are illuminated). Explore the hip bar and restaurant scene along the canal.

meals.breakfast: Log Road Daikanyama or Ivy Place café — brunch-style breakfast in a beautiful garden setting (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills food floor or a bento from a nearby depachika (¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Nakameguro canal-side restaurant — Nakameguro Taproom (craft beer and food) or a Japanese-Italian fusion bistro along the river (¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Mori Art Museum often has world-class contemporary exhibitions — check the current show online before visiting. Nakameguro is extremely popular on Saturday evenings — arrive by 18:00 to get a good riverside spot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Digital Art Museum (if not visited on Day 5) or explore the Shiodome/Shimbashi area — visit the Panasonic Center Tokyo or Sony Park for free tech culture experiences. Alternatively, visit the Intermediatheque (free museum in KITTE building near Tokyo Station) for natural history and science exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the KITTE shopping mall (inside a beautifully converted historic post office building) and Tokyo Station's Gransta underground food complex — one of the best places to buy ekiben (train station bento) and Japanese food souvenirs. Visit the Tokyo Station Gallery for art.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening — head to the Tokyo Tower area (Shiba Park) for a classic Tokyo icon. Climb Tokyo Tower (Main Deck ¥1,200) for nostalgic views. Finish with a special farewell dinner in the upscale Azabu-Juban neighborhood nearby.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market one final time — fresh seafood breakfast bowl and tamagoyaki (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.lunch: KITTE Marunouchi food floor or Tokyo Station ramen street (Ramen Street in the basement) — try Fuunji tsukemen (dipping ramen) (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Azabu-Juban — Torishiki (yakitori omakase, book in advance) or a traditional Japanese restaurant for a memorable farewell dinner (¥4,000–¥7,000)

day_by_day.notes: KITTE's rooftop terrace (free) offers a unique view directly onto Tokyo Station's iconic red-brick facade — great for photos. Stock up on food souvenirs at Tokyo Station's Gransta — it has the best selection of regional Japanese snacks and sweets.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a peaceful early walk along the Tsukiji waterfront and Harumi Wharf area for reflective views of Tokyo Bay. Visit any remaining Tsukiji Outer Market stalls for a final fresh sushi breakfast and last-minute food souvenirs (dried seaweed, dashi packs, wasabi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to hotel, check out, and pack. Head to Tokyo Station or Shinjuku Station for the Narita Express or Airport Limousine Bus. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before flight departure for international travel. Browse the airport duty-free for Japanese whisky, cosmetics, and Kit Kat flavors.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Sayonara!

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — omakase sushi or a fresh seafood don at Tsukiji Sushi Sen (¥2,000–¥3,500)
meals.lunch: Airport lunch at Narita or Haneda — try the airport ramen or soba restaurant for a final Japanese meal (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — arrange luggage storage at the hotel if needed for a few extra hours. Narita Express (N'EX) takes about 60 minutes from Tokyo Station; allow extra time on Monday mornings due to business travel. Keep some yen for last-minute purchases as not all airport shops accept foreign cards.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's culinary soul.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from Narita/Haneda to Tsukiji boutique hotel via private luxury car service. Check-in, freshen up, and orient yourself to the Tsukiji neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Tsukiji Outer Market for a self-guided introduction – sample fresh tamagoyaki, uni, and grilled scallops from renowned stalls. Visit nearby Namiyoke Inari Shrine for a calm, culturally rich moment before the evening begins.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito (reservation essential, arrange in advance) or Kyubey Ginza – one of Tokyo's most celebrated sushi counters, just minutes from Tsukiji. Experience an omakase course featuring the freshest seasonal fish.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight
meals.lunch: Light snacks at Tsukiji Outer Market stalls (tamagoyaki, fresh oysters, tuna skewers) – budget ¥3,000–5,000
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi at Kyubey Ginza or equivalent high-end sushi counter – budget ¥30,000–50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer. Confirm omakase dinner reservation well in advance – top Tokyo sushi counters book 1–3 months ahead. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to adjust quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (guided premium experience): Explore the market's labyrinthine lanes with a knowledgeable local guide. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, Japanese pickles, dashi broth, and seasonal street snacks. Visit specialty vendors for premium tuna, wagyu, and rare Japanese pantry items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ginza – Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district, a 10-minute walk from Tsukiji. Visit the flagship stores of Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons, and the iconic Itoya stationery boutique. Explore the Ginza Six luxury mall and its rooftop garden with city views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) if reservations were secured, or dine at Robinhood Ginza for premium wagyu shabu-shabu. Afterward, enjoy cocktails at the Mandarin Oriental Bar in nearby Nihonbashi.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Tsukiji Outer Market fresh fruit, tamagoyaki, and green tea – budget ¥2,000–3,000
meals.lunch: Premium sushi bento or kaisendon (seafood rice bowl) at a top Tsukiji restaurant such as Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi – budget ¥5,000–8,000
meals.dinner: Wagyu shabu-shabu or omakase at a Ginza fine-dining establishment – budget ¥25,000–45,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant 07:00–11:00; the morning tour takes full advantage of this. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone market lanes. Ginza stores open around 11:00–12:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit teamLab Planets (Toyosu, 15 minutes by taxi) – an immersive digital art museum merging tech culture and aesthetic wonder. Walk through water-filled rooms, infinite flower gardens, and mirrored light installations. Book timed-entry tickets in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toyosu Market (adjacent to teamLab) – the world's largest wholesale fish market. Take a premium guided tour of the tuna auction observation deck and inner market facilities. Return to Tsukiji area and visit the Hamarikyu Gardens – a stunning Edo-era landscape garden with a traditional teahouse on the water.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Narisawa (Minami-Aoyama, 20 minutes by taxi) – consistently ranked among Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, blending Japanese cuisine with innovative techniques inspired by nature. A landmark fine-dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café au lait and a morning pastry at Café de l'Ambre in Ginza – Tokyo's legendary old-school coffee shop
meals.lunch: Ramen at Fuunji (Shinjuku) or a premium bento from a Toyosu market vendor – budget ¥2,000–4,000
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Narisawa – budget ¥40,000–60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets requires advance timed-entry booking – purchase tickets on the official website. Hamarikyu Gardens entry is ¥300. Narisawa reservations should be made 1–2 months in advance via their official website.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akihabara – Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Explore multi-floor electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, Bic Camera), specialist retro gaming shops, and cutting-edge gadget boutiques. Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan for rare tech collectibles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara: visit the Gundam Café, explore high-end audiophile shops, and browse the latest Japanese tech innovations. Then head to Kanda Myojin Shrine – one of Tokyo's oldest shrines, historically the patron of IT companies, featuring a fascinating blend of Shinto tradition and modern tech culture (IT ema prayer boards).
day_by_day.evening: Cross into Ueno for dinner at Ueno Seiyoken – a historic Western-style restaurant operating since 1876, offering classic yoshoku (Japanese-Western fusion) cuisine. Stroll through Ueno Park in the evening if cherry blossoms are still present in mid-April.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee and toast at a specialty café near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Akihabara maid café experience (cultural immersion) or premium ramen at Fuunji nearby – budget ¥2,000–4,000
meals.dinner: Yoshoku course dinner at Ueno Seiyoken or kaiseki at Hantei in Nezu – budget ¥15,000–25,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is extremely busy on weekends – arrive early. Many shops open around 10:00–11:00. Kanda Myojin is free to enter. Mid-April may still offer late cherry blossoms in Ueno Park – a spectacular bonus.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa (20 minutes from Tsukiji by taxi or subway). Arrive early (08:00) to experience the temple before crowds arrive. Walk the Nakamise shopping street for traditional crafts, ningyo-yaki sweets, and premium wagashi. Explore the Asakusa Shrine and surrounding historic lanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo Skytree (adjacent to Asakusa) – at 634 meters, the world's tallest tower. Ascend to the Tembo Galleria (450m) for panoramic views over Tokyo. Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at its base, featuring Japanese design, food, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ryugin (Roppongi) – a three-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurant led by Chef Seiji Yamamoto, celebrated for reinterpreting Japanese culinary tradition with extraordinary precision. One of Tokyo's most prestigious dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the hotel or a warm bowl of soba near Asakusa
meals.lunch: Premium tempura at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa (est. 1887) or a kaisendon at a Solamachi restaurant – budget ¥5,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Kaiseki tasting menu at Ryugin – budget ¥45,000–65,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and most atmospheric at dawn. Tokyo Skytree tickets can be purchased in advance online to skip queues. Ryugin reservations must be made well in advance – use Tableall or Tablecheck platforms.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku and Omotesando: Begin at Meiji Jingu Shrine for a serene forest walk and Shinto ceremony viewing. Then stroll down Omotesando – Tokyo's most elegant boulevard – lined with architectural masterpieces housing Louis Vuitton, Prada, and Dior flagship stores designed by world-renowned architects.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Omotesando Hills complex (designed by Tadao Ando) for luxury shopping and gallery spaces. Explore the Nezu Museum – a world-class collection of Asian art set within a stunning bamboo garden. Finish in Aoyama's gallery district for contemporary Japanese art.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at L'Effervescence (Nishi-Azabu) – a two-Michelin-star restaurant by Chef Shinobu Namae, offering a brilliant fusion of French technique and Japanese philosophy. Afterward, enjoy cocktails at the Bar High Five in Ginza – one of the world's most celebrated cocktail bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or specialty pour-over coffee and croissant at Bear Pond Espresso or Fuglen Tokyo in Tomigaya
meals.lunch: Japanese crêpes and Harajuku street food experience, or a refined lunch at Pierre Hermé Paris Aoyama – budget ¥3,000–6,000
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at L'Effervescence – budget ¥35,000–55,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter; arrive before 09:00 for a peaceful experience. Nezu Museum entry is ¥1,300. Bar High Five is intimate – reservations recommended. Omotesando boutiques open at 11:00.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba – Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island. Visit the teamLab Borderless digital art museum (recently relocated to Azabudai Hills – confirm current location) for a full-day immersive tech-art experience. Alternatively, explore the Miraikan National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation, featuring ASIMO robots, space exploration exhibits, and cutting-edge Japanese technology displays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (featuring a life-size Gundam statue) and the Venus Fort shopping mall with its faux-European interior. Visit the Palette Town area and enjoy views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline from Odaiba seaside park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo for dinner at Sushi Yoshitake (Ginza) – a three-Michelin-star sushi counter offering an extraordinary omakase experience with rare seasonal ingredients and masterful Edomae technique.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or fresh morning pastry at a Tsukiji-area bakery
meals.lunch: Ramen or tonkatsu at a premium Odaiba restaurant – budget ¥3,000–6,000
meals.dinner: Omakase at Sushi Yoshitake – budget ¥40,000–60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Odaiba is accessible via the scenic Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi (15 minutes). Miraikan tickets can be purchased online. teamLab Borderless tickets sell out – book weeks in advance. Check current venue location before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku: Start at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, opens 09:00) for sweeping city views. Explore the Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden – one of Japan's most beautiful parks, ideal for late cherry blossom viewing in mid-April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's Takashimaya Times Square department store for premium Japanese goods, food halls, and designer boutiques. Visit Isetan Shinjuku – Japan's most prestigious department store – for its extraordinary basement food hall (depachika) featuring premium wagyu, artisan sweets, and regional Japanese delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku at night: walk through the neon-lit Kabukicho entertainment district, visit the atmospheric Golden Gai (tiny bars in historic wooden buildings), and enjoy cocktails at the New York Bar in the Park Hyatt Shinjuku (made famous by Lost in Translation).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a local kissaten (coffee shop)
meals.lunch: Premium kaiseki bento or soba course at Isetan's top-floor restaurant – budget ¥5,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki wagyu dinner at Shinjuku Misono or Ukai-tei Shinjuku – budget ¥25,000–40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry is ¥500; alcohol is not permitted inside. Golden Gai bars are tiny and intimate – many welcome tourists; look for English-friendly signage. Park Hyatt New York Bar has a cover charge after 20:00 (¥2,200).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills – one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art institutions with rotating world-class exhibitions. Ascend to the Tokyo City View observation deck for 360-degree panoramas. Explore the Roppongi Hills complex, designed by Minoru Mori as a city-within-a-city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi – Japan's largest exhibition space featuring rotating contemporary art shows in a stunning wave-form glass building designed by Kisho Kurokawa. Explore the nearby Suntory Museum of Art for traditional Japanese decorative arts.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Azabu Kadowaki (Azabu-Juban) – a two-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurant celebrated for its exquisite seasonal ingredients and intimate atmosphere. Afterward, explore the upscale Azabu-Juban neighborhood's boutique bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee at Switch Coffee Tokyo
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at the National Art Center's Brasserie Paul Bocuse Le Musée – a French restaurant inside the museum – budget ¥5,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Kaiseki at Azabu Kadowaki – budget ¥35,000–55,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is open until 22:00 on most days – check current hours. The National Art Center is closed on Tuesdays. Roppongi Hills Mori Tower observation deck tickets can be combined with museum entry.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka – one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic neighborhoods, largely untouched by WWII bombing. Wander the Yanaka Ginza shopping street, visit the atmospheric Yanaka Cemetery (famous for cherry blossoms), and browse independent galleries, craft studios, and traditional shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno – Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing the world's most extensive collection of Japanese art and artifacts. Highlights include samurai armor, ukiyo-e prints, ancient ceramics, and Buddhist sculpture. The Honkan (Japanese Gallery) alone warrants 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Kanda (Minami-Aoyama) – a three-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurant led by Chef Hiroyuki Kanda, revered for its pure, understated Japanese culinary philosophy. One of the most exclusive dining experiences in the world.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or fresh coffee and pastry at a Yanaka neighborhood café
meals.lunch: Menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet) or traditional wagashi sweets at Yanaka Ginza stalls, followed by a light café lunch – budget ¥2,000–4,000
meals.dinner: Kaiseki at Kanda – budget ¥50,000–70,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum entry is ¥1,000; special exhibitions cost extra. Yanaka is best explored on foot – wear comfortable shoes. Kanda restaurant is one of the hardest reservations in Tokyo – book 2–3 months in advance via Tableall.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Nikko Limited Express from Asakusa). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex – an extraordinarily ornate mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, surrounded by ancient cedar forest. Explore Rinnoji Temple and Futarasan Shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: walk to Kegon Falls (one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls) and stroll around Lake Chuzenji. In late April, the surrounding mountains may still feature snow-capped peaks alongside spring blossoms – a breathtaking contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo (arrive ~19:00). Dinner at Ishikawa (Kagurazaka) – a three-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurant in a beautiful traditional townhouse setting. Chef Hideki Ishikawa's cuisine is celebrated for its warmth, depth, and exceptional seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick onigiri and green tea from a Tsukiji convenience store before departure
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a Nikko specialty restaurant – a regional delicacy – budget ¥3,000–6,000
meals.dinner: Kaiseki at Ishikawa – budget ¥40,000–60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Tobu Nikko Pass for unlimited train and bus travel in the Nikko area. Tosho-gu entry is ¥1,300. Depart Tokyo by 08:00 to maximize time in Nikko. Nikko can be cold in April – bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Azabudai Hills complex – Tokyo's newest and most ambitious urban development (opened 2023), featuring the Mori JP Tower (tallest building in Japan), the Azabudai Hills Gallery, premium boutiques, and extraordinary architecture by Heatherwick Studio. Explore the rooftop gardens and public art installations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sony Park and Sony Showroom in Ginza – an interactive tech showcase displaying Sony's latest innovations, concept products, and immersive experiences. Then browse the Itoya flagship stationery store (9 floors of premium Japanese paper goods, pens, and design objects) and the Ginza Six luxury mall.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium dinner at Quintessence (Shirokanedai) – a three-Michelin-star French restaurant by Chef Shuzo Kishida, offering a masterful interpretation of French cuisine through Japanese precision. One of the most refined dining experiences in Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or brunch at bills Omotesando – the legendary Australian brunch spot with premium Japanese ingredients
meals.lunch: Premium tonkatsu at Butagumi in Nishi-Azabu (using rare heritage pork breeds) or a refined lunch at a Ginza café – budget ¥5,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Quintessence – budget ¥40,000–60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Azabudai Hills is a short taxi ride from Tsukiji. Sony Showroom is free to enter. Quintessence serves only one seating per evening – confirm reservation details carefully. This is an ideal night for reflection on the trip's culinary journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tsukiji: revisit the Outer Market for a farewell breakfast of fresh sushi and tamagoyaki. Purchase premium Japanese souvenirs – high-grade matcha, artisan dashi packs, wagashi sweets, and specialty condiments from the market's finest vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration: visit the Hamarikyu Gardens for a peaceful farewell stroll and traditional tea ceremony at the Nakajima Teahouse (¥700, served with wagashi). Return to the hotel for final packing and checkout. Arrange private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If time permits before the flight, explore the premium duty-free shopping at Narita Airport – excellent for last-minute wagyu jerky, sake, Japanese whisky (Yamazaki, Hibiki), and artisan ceramics.

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market (Daiwa Sushi or Sushi Dai) – budget ¥5,000–8,000
meals.lunch: Light bento or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: In-flight or airport dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in and security. Narita Airport is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo by Narita Express; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Consider shipping purchased goods home via Japan Post's Takkyubin service to avoid luggage issues. Sayonara, Tokyo!
